title: Representing a connecting map and attaching the top projective term
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe and let $C$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(C)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ with localization $Q$, cochain shifts and cones [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix integers $a<b$, an object $P\in\mathcal A$, an object $M\in D(\mathcal A)$, and a complex $Q^\bullet$ which is zero outside $[a,b-1]$ and has projective terms (maps from each term lift along epimorphisms). Suppose a distinguished triangle is given:
$$P[-b]\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Q(Q^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1].$$
Write $P[-b+1]$ also for the actual single-term complex with $P$ in degree $b-1$. There is a chain map $g:Q^\bullet\to P[-b+1]$ representing $\delta$ in the derived category. Its only possibly nonzero component is $g^{b-1}:Q^{b-1}\to P$, and it satisfies $g^{b-1}d_Q^{b-2}=0$. The complex $D^\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(g)[-1]$ represents $M$. Under the evident term identifications it has terms $Q^q$ for $q<b$, term $P$ in degree $b$, and zero terms outside $[a,b]$; its last differential is $g^{b-1}$ with the sign fixed by the cone and shift convention. In particular, if $P$ and all $Q^q$ are finite free $C$-module sheaves, then so are all terms of $D^\bullet$. The rank-zero case $P=0$ is included. No constancy of entries of $g^{b-1}$ is required.
